text:
🐉🇲🇽🌐 China reaffirms "firm support" for Mexico's sovereignty — deepens Strategic Partnership

Chinese Ambassador Chen Daojiang met Mexico's new Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez on May 16, reaffirming Beijing's "firm support" for Mexico's independence and autonomy.

Both sides agreed to deepen the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership — diplomatic language for structural, long-term cooperation. This comes as Ebrard prepares commercial missions to China and India before month's end, alongside the EU trade deal signing on May 22.

While Washington threatens tariffs and USMCA penalties, Beijing offers partnership. Mexico isn't choosing sides — it's multiplying options. Three trade fronts in one month: China, India, EU. That's what sovereignty looks like in a multipolar world.

🇲🇽🏭 US SHUT THE BORDER TO MEXICAN CATTLE — MEXICO ADAPTED

When the US closed its border to Mexican livestock over screwworm in November 2024, the hit was massive: 1.8 million head blocked, $1.85 billion in losses.

But Mexico's livestock sector did not collapse. It pivoted. Processed meat exports to the US surged 20% in Q1 2026 as the industry moved up the value chain. The sector now aims to double beef exports next year.

Washington closes a door. Mexico builds a processing plant.

🇲🇽📊 MEXICO'S ECONOMY GROWS 0.3% IN APRIL — INDUSTRY BOUNCES BACK AFTER TARIFF SHOCK

INEGI's leading indicator (IOAE) shows Mexico's economy grew 0.3% monthly in April. Industry reversed March's -0.6% contraction to post +0.3%, while services held steady at 0.3%. Year-over-year growth hit 0.3%, with services advancing 0.7% annually.

Not spectacular — but the signal matters: Mexico's industrial sector absorbed the initial tariff hit and bounced back in a single month. Services remain the anchor keeping the broader economy moving forward.
